scope: Proposition 18.5 (Joint endpoint kernels) of the manuscript “The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order” (preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 171 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7d4b26e897038267), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 159-160. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed tuple of positions just described there are deterministic nonnegative symmetric pair weights Hv, chosen before endpoint values, such that every assignment of two endpoints per row satisfies Pr(specified pairs, full run) ≤ eO(r) Kt′ exp(.01nm + C′ t′ j) Y v Hv(xv, zv), (18.5) where C′ is fixed and the nonnegative symmetric kernels on palette labels (allowing different kernels according to the positions) satisfy sup x X z Hv(x, z) ≤ K/M, max Hv ≤ M−2 e.01n . 159 In particular we can use Hv = M−2 on nonisolates.
